response.message:
We're building an AWS triage pipeline for synthetic security alerts. It goes ingest → redact → retrieve evidence → AI triage → analyst queue, and it ends with an auditable response proposal. Nothing acts on its own: no host isolation, no user disabling and no payload execution. I've drawn the full flow with real service names. These AWS services aren't covered by native code generation yet, so they'll need engineering work, and no region, account or deployment has been verified.

**First local test:** we push a synthetic alert through in emulation. It should be redacted, matched to evidence and land in the case table with a proposal and an audit record. The model's reply in that test is a scripted stand-in. It shows the wiring works, not how good the triage is. Checking real triage quality needs a separate run against a chosen Bedrock model, scored on labelled synthetic alerts.

Which country does this alert and log data need to stay in? That answer will guide which region we propose.

data.description: Existing producer of synthetic security alerts. Outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Raw alert landing
data.description: Private, versioned, encrypted bucket for raw alerts. Restricted access, and object-created events go to the ingest queue.

data.label: Ingest queue
data.description: Buffers alerts for redaction. Visibility timeout is at least 6x the function timeout.

data.label: Ingest dead-letter queue
data.description: Holds alerts that repeatedly fail, with an alarm for the operator.

data.label: Redaction function
data.description: Reads the exact object version, masks sensitive fields (user names, IPs, secrets) using rules, writes the redacted alert and starts the workflow. Idempotent per version.

data.label: Redacted alert store
data.description: Private encrypted bucket for redacted alerts that downstream steps are allowed to read.

data.label: Triage workflow
data.description: Orchestrates evidence retrieval, AI triage, case creation and audit writes. It has no action permissions on hosts or identities.

data.label: Asset inventory
data.description: Existing asset context (owner, criticality). Read-only, and the integration is to be defined.

data.label: Approved log evidence
data.description: Index of approved, redacted logs searched by time window and entity.

data.label: Evidence retrieval
data.description: Read-only queries for related logs and asset context. Returns cited evidence references.

data.label: AI triage
data.description: Builds a bounded prompt from the redacted alert and evidence, treating evidence as untrusted. Returns severity, rationale, citations and a proposal-only response. The output schema is validated.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: Model not yet selected. Access, region availability and quotas are unverified.

data.label: Analyst case queue
data.description: Triage cases with status (new/accepted/rejected), proposal and evidence links. Analysts record decisions here.

data.label: Audit record store
data.description: Bucket with Object Lock holding immutable records: alert ID, evidence references, model ID, prompt version, proposal and analyst decision.

data.label: Security analyst
data.description: Reviews proposals and decides. Any action is taken manually outside this system.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Makes AI recommendations reviewable and reproducible during investigations.

response.message:
We have **no failed checks**, and no wiring broke in the local emulation of the design you drew. The run is still **blocked** for two reasons:

- **Five components have no generated code yet.** The ingest queue, dead-letter queue, redaction function, triage workflow and the import plan for your existing alert source can't be generated by the tool today. That's product engineering work, not a design mistake. Editing the diagram won't fix it, and we should keep all five rather than remove them to clear the check.
- **The first thing we can fix in the design:** the raw alert bucket doesn't say who is allowed to put alerts into it. The redacted store and the audit store have the same gap, and we can handle them next.

The fix for the raw bucket would mark your alert producer as an existing AWS identity and give its upload link an access level. The catch is that the tool only offers "read" or "read and write" for that link. There is no "write-only" option.

That matters here because the raw bucket holds unredacted, confidential alerts. If the producer only needs to upload, giving it read access would let it read every raw alert. That breaks the rule that unredacted payloads stay restricted. So I haven't changed the diagram until we know which you need.

Once you've made a change, run the emulation again on the new export. This result doesn't carry over to a changed design.

Is the synthetic alert producer an IAM role in the same AWS account, and does it only need to upload alerts, or does it also need to read them back?
